What differs between recovery and ordinary insertion, and why reads still work\n\n**Ordinary insertion (process A, pre-crash).** `CollectionImpl::write_impl` → `handle_insert` → `SegmentImpl::Insert` (`src/db/index/segment/segment.cc:903-918`): each doc is first appended to the WAL via `append_wal` (`segment.cc:4324-4340`), which **lazily creates/opens the member `wal_file_`** on first write, then `internal_insert` (`segment.cc:837-881`) populates the RAM structures: `id_map_`, `memory_store_` (forward rows), scalar/FTS/vector memory indexers, the in-memory writing-block meta (`max_doc_id_`, `doc_count_`, lines 874-876), and `doc_ids_` (line 878). So in normal operation the invariant holds: *data in the memory block ⟺ `wal_file_` attached with records on disk*.\n\n**Recovery (process B).** `CollectionImpl::Open` with no schema calls `recovery()` (`src/db/collection.cc:308-323, 1836-1892`): it loads the highest-numbered `MANIFEST.<n>` (`src/db/index/common/version_manager.cc:190-241`), opens persisted segments read-only (collection.cc:1861-1874), then opens the writing segment (collection.cc:1879-1887). In `SegmentImpl::Open`, WAL replay happens **only if the segment meta has a writing forward block** (`segment.cc:484-501`). `SegmentImpl::recover()` (`segment.cc:4193-4301`) opens the WAL file `<coll>/<seg_id>/<block_id>.wal` (`src/db/common/file_helper.h:74-79`) with a **separate, local read handle** `recover_wal_file` that is closed on exit (segment.cc:4206-4215), and replays each record through `internal_insert/internal_update/internal_upsert/internal_delete` (segment.cc:4250-4266) — deliberately bypassing `append_wal` so records aren't duplicated. It then bumps `mem_block.max_doc_id_` **in memory only** (segment.cc:4285-4288); the manifest's copy of the writing block still says `doc_count 0`, and no version update/flush occurs.\n\n**The differing state:** after recovery the memory block is full (docs, indexers, `doc_ids_`, id-map), the WAL file still exists on disk, but the segment's `wal_file_` member is `nullptr` — the invariant above is broken. (Side observation: in the replay loop, `status` at segment.cc:4249 is never assigned by the `internal_*` calls, so the error check at 4274-4280 is dead — replay failures would be silently ignored. Not causal here, but symptomatic of this path's rigor.)\n\n**Why reads work:** everything read-side is RAM-based. `SegmentImpl::doc_count()` is `doc_ids_.size()` (`segment.cc:589-600`); `get_all_segments()` includes the writing segment whenever `doc_count() > 0` (`collection.cc:2076-2082`); `Stats()` sums those counts (`collection.cc:403-442`); `Fetch`/`Query` resolve via `id_map_` + `local_segment_by_doc_id` against the writing block's in-memory `min/max_doc_id` (updated at segment.cc:4288) and read `memory_store_` (`collection.cc:1376-1401`). So count/fetch succeed in process B purely from replayed memory state.\n\n## 2. The call sequence and exact condition under which `Optimize()` succeeds and loses the data\n\nIn process B, `Optimize()` (`collection.cc:779-915`) with no new inserts:\n\n1. **`collection.cc:794`** — `writing_segment_->doc_count() != 0` is **true** (RAM count from replay), so it calls `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing()` (collection.cc:796). Since the no-op flush persisted no blocks, this \"persisted\" segment's meta now has **zero SCALAR blocks and no writing block** → `SegmentMeta::doc_count() == 0` (`src/db/index/common/meta.h:307-318`).\n5. **`collection.cc:1546-1549`** — `version_manager_->apply(version)` + `flush()`: writes `MANIFEST.<n+1>` and **deletes `MANIFEST.<n>`** (`version_manager.cc:282-301`). Back in `Optimize`: `persist_segments = [seg0]` (collection.cc:802-803), so it does not take the empty early-return (807-810). `build_compact_task` on a single small segment with no delete pressure produces a `CreateVectorIndexTask` (collection.cc:991-1001). With the default FLAT params (`src/include/zvec/db/index_params.h:437`; FLAT fields are marked indexed at segment creation, `segment.cc:534-539`), `create_vector_index` short-circuits as \"already indexed, same params\" (`segment.cc:1685-1690`) — or, for a non-default index, `merge_vector_indexer` merges the (empty) *persisted* indexer list (`segment.cc:1711-1727`) — either way it **succeeds**. The output meta is folded in via `update_persisted_segment_meta` (collection.cc:863-867), `apply` + `flush` commit again (872-877), `reload_vector_index` updates the in-memory segment (902-909), and `Optimize` returns `Status::OK()` (914).\n7. **Why the WAL can't save it on reopen:** the seg0 WAL file was never removed (removal lives only inside the skipped flush path, segment.cc:2305-2315), but it is now an orphan: replay happens only for the version's *writing* segment (collection.cc:1879-1885) and only when its meta has a writing block (segment.cc:484-501). The segment reclassified at collection.cc:1538-1539 genuinely contains persisted blocks, so reopen finds the docs.\n\n## 3. Why success and same-handle stats prove nothing here\n\n- **`Optimize`'s OK is real but hollow.** Every operation it *performed* (task execution, renames, version apply/flush) did succeed. The durability step failed by *silently doing nothing* and returning `Status::OK()` (segment.cc:2220-2222). \"OK\" from flush means \"there was nothing to flush\" under the broken handle-liveness check, not \"data is on disk.\" Note the same applies to an explicit `Flush()` in process B (collection.cc:380-395) — it also returns OK as a no-op.\n- **Stats read RAM, reopen reads the manifest.** `Stats()` (collection.cc:403-442) sums `doc_ids_.size()` over `get_all_segments()` (collection.cc:2076-2082), which still includes the sealed seg0 object held alive by `segment_manager_` with its `memory_store_` and `doc_ids_` intact; `index_completeness` reads `meta()->vector_indexed(...)` (collection.cc:433), which optimize just set to true (segment.cc:1685-1691 + collection.cc:863-867, 902-909). None of this touches disk. Process C rebuilds state exclusively from `MANIFEST.<max>` (version_manager.cc:205-241) and the persisted block files listed in it (segment.cc:461-517, `load_persist_scalar_blocks`) — which describe zero documents. Same-handle statistics therefore measure exactly the state that dies with the process.\n\n## 4. Smallest repair principle, and a regression test that would catch it\n\n**Repair principle (one sentence):** a memory block repopulated by WAL replay must be treated as dirty — i.e., restore the invariant *\"WAL file for the current memory block exists ⟺ segment holds unpersisted data covered by it, and `flush()` is the only thing allowed to end that state.\"*\n\nSmallest concrete shape (describe-only): at the end of the recovery branch of `SegmentImpl::Open` / `recover()` (segment.cc:490-501, 4193-4301), when a WAL file was found and replayed, **re-attach it** by calling the existing `open_wal_file()` (segment.cc:4303-4322), which opens the existing file in append mode (`local_wal_file.cc:92-106`). Then the untouched `flush()` gate at segment.cc:2220 sees `has_record() == true`, and the existing full path does everything required *in the right order*: persist memory components (4342-4412) → commit meta to a new manifest (`update_version`, 4414-4426) → only then remove the WAL (2305-2315). No changes needed in `Optimize`, `dump()`, or `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing`. (An equally small alternative is to change the 2220 condition to test memory-block state — e.g. `memory_store_ != nullptr` / writing-block `doc_count_ != 0` — but then the WAL-removal step must also handle a never-attached file, so re-attachment is the smaller diff.) A cheap defensive guard, beyond the minimum: before `remove_writing_forward_block()`/`add_persisted_segment_meta` (collection.cc:1538-1539), assert the sealed meta's `doc_count()` equals the in-memory `doc_count()` — this class of bug then fails loudly instead of losing data.\n\n**Regression-test sequence** (fits the existing harness in `tests/db/crash_recovery/`, which already fork/SIGKILLs child binaries — `optimize_recovery_test.cc:52-118`, `write_recovery_test.cc`):\n\n1. **Phase 1 (child, killed):** `CreateAndOpen` at a temp path; `Insert` N docs (N small — no buffer/segment rollover); terminate with `SIGKILL`/`_exit` **without** `Flush()` and without graceful `reset()` — a graceful close would run `close_unsafe → flush` (collection.cc:340-361) with an attached WAL and persist everything, masking the bug. (This is exactly the hole in the current `CrashDuringOptimize` test: it does a graceful `collection.reset()` at `optimize_recovery_test.cc:164` *before* crashing the optimizer, and after its recovery reopen it *inserts more docs* at lines 207-219 — which re-attaches `wal_file_` via `append_wal` — before running the optimizer at 223. The recovery→optimize-with-no-intervening-write window is never exercised.)\n2. **Phase 2 (new process):** `Collection::Open`; assert `Stats().doc_count == N` and `Fetch(all pks)` returns N docs (recovery works); then `Optimize()` and assert OK; optionally re-assert `Stats().doc_count == N` on the same handle (passes even when buggy — that's the point); close gracefully.\n3. **Phase 3 (new process):** `Collection::Open`; assert `Stats().doc_count == N`, `Fetch` returns all N docs byte-equal, and a top-k `Query` hits. **This is the assertion that fails pre-fix (count 0) and passes post-fix.**\n4.
